newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon's MEA leases four jets to upgrade fleet.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon's MEA leases four jets to upgrade fleet.

text.p: Lebanon's flag carrier Middle East Airlines (MEA) said on Friday it had leased four new Airbus planes and plans to lease four more to upgrade its ailing fleet.

"We have signed this contract. The first plane will arrive from the Airbus factory in Hamburg at the start of the new year, then two will arrive in March and another one in April," MEA chairman Khaled Salam told reporters.
"This will be followed by the leasing of four other planes, so the total will be eight planes. All of this is within the context of rehabilitating the company and upgrading its fleet," he added.
In July, MEA launched an operation to increase its capital by $225 million, to rehabilitate the airline, upgrade its 14-plane fleet and pay its $100-million debt.

Shareholders carried out a $100 million debt for equity swap as the first stage of the rise -- 90 percent of the shares were taken by the central bank -- and a second capital rise of $125 million will be agreed at a shareholders meeting in October.

MEA flourished before the 1975-90 Lebanese civil war but the fighting and the devaluation of the local currency have reduced its 150 million pound capital to $96,000 before the capital increase in July.
